data.title: Dual Drug Approvals Could Be A Big Moment For Sanofi Stock (ENXTPA:SAN)
data.description:

  • These green lights expand Sanofi's reach in both global vaccination programs and rare disease treatment. They add fresh products in areas where clinical need is high and where the group has already built meaningful manufacturing, regulatory and commercial know how.

The fresh FDA approval for Infilbray looks most relevant for catalysts because it fits directly into Sanofi’s rare disease and neurology focus that investors already watch closely. It is a once daily oral option for neurological manifestations of Type 3 Gaucher disease, a space with few alternatives, and it runs across both adult and pediatric patients.

data.title: Arista Networks (ANET) Dropped, But What Is The Market Weighing Now?
data.description:
Arista Networks (ANET) just paired rapid Q3 2026 revenue and earnings expansion with the launch of new Etherlink R4 platforms, tying recent financial strength directly to fresh AI inferencing hardware.

Arista Networks’ share price has pulled back sharply despite the upbeat Q3 release. The stock is down 11.6% over the past day and 15.0% over the last week. Even so, its year-to-date share price return of 25.5% sits alongside a 1-year total shareholder return of 42.7% and a roughly 4.4x 5-year total shareholder return. This highlights longer-term momentum even as short-term sentiment cools in response to profit taking and growing debate about future AI infrastructure spending.

Scan beyond Arista Networks and see how other AI infrastructure plays are lining up by reviewing our hand picked 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

After a drop like this, some investors will be tempted to treat Arista Networks as a quick bargain, while others would rather sit tight for an even cheaper entry. Where does the current valuation actually leave you?

Most Popular Narrative: 1% Undervalued

On the latest view, the narrative fair value of Arista Networks at $169.91 sits only slightly above the last close of $167.62. That small gap puts the focus squarely on how sustainable the current AI buildout looks rather than on any big pricing mismatch.

Arista reported Q3 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 58.5%, and forecast Q4 revenue between $3.9 billion and $4 billion. The headline is strong. One table in the 10-Q adds a detail worth holding next to it. Deferred revenue fell in the quarter, from $6,865.9 million to $6,839.5 million. A year earlier it rose $624.5 million. Revenue recognized from the opening deferred balance was $1,715.0 million, about 47% of Q3 revenue, against $699.7 million, about 30%, in Q3 2025. That balance holds multi-year support contracts and product deferrals tied to acceptance clauses. When large customers accept deployments, revenue comes out of it, so part of Q3's growth likely came from earlier shipments clearing rather than only from new orders. New deferrals were still $1,688.6 million, up from $1,324.2 million a year earlier. The balance is being refilled, just not faster than it's being drawn down. The CFO warned against reading one quarter too closely: "the deferred balance can move significantly on a quarterly basis, independent of underlying business drivers." I agree, and this isn't a bear case. Management's first look at 2027 is 38% to 40% growth, to about $18.5 billion. Arista expects $8.6 billion of revenue from remaining performance obligations, about 91% of it within two years, and purchase commitments rose to $11.4 billion from $9.7 billion in Q2. What I'd watch in the Q4 report is whether the balance grows again. If it does alongside revenue of $3.9 billion or more, demand is outrunning acceptances. If it falls again, growth is leaning harder on the balance, and the 2027 range carries more of the story. The Q3 call and both filings are here. On the fair value: the form needs a number, so I set it at the last close on purpose. This is a view on the report, not a long-term valuation. Data: Arista's 10-Q and Q3 call, processed by Equibles. Equibles staff may hold positions in the securities discussed. This is my analysis of public filings, not a recommendation.

Result: Fair Value of $169.91 (ABOUT RIGHT)

Still, this story can change quickly if large customers slow AI data center rollouts or if deferred revenue continues shrinking relative to reported sales.

Look at the same Arista Networks chart through earnings and the picture tightens. The stock trades on a P/E of 44.6x, compared with 23.9x for the US Communications sector, 37.3x for peers, and a 38.5x fair ratio that the market could eventually lean back toward.

For example, although Amazon.com made losses for many years after listing, if you had bought and held the shares since 1999, you would have made a fortune. But while history lauds those rare successes, those that fail are often forgotten; who remembers Pets.com?

So should Pioneer Power Solutions (NASDAQ:PPSI) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? For the purpose of this article, we'll define cash burn as the amount of cash the company is spending each year to fund its growth (also called its negative free cash flow). We'll start by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves in order to calculate its cash runway.

When Might Pioneer Power Solutions Run Out Of Money?

A cash runway is defined as the length of time it would take a company to run out of money if it kept spending at its current rate of cash burn. As at September 2026, Pioneer Power Solutions had cash of US$9.4m and no debt. Importantly, its cash burn was US$8.1m over the trailing twelve months. So it had a cash runway of approximately 14 months from September 2026. That's not too bad, but it's fair to say the end of the cash runway is in sight, unless cash burn reduces drastically. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

Check out our latest analysis for Pioneer Power Solutions

How Well Is Pioneer Power Solutions Growing?

We reckon the fact that Pioneer Power Solutions managed to shrink its cash burn by 26% over the last year is rather encouraging. Unfortunately, however, operating revenue declined by 37% during the period. In light of the data above, we're fairly sanguine about the business growth trajectory. Clearly, however, the crucial factor is whether the company will grow its business going forward. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

Can Pioneer Power Solutions Raise More Cash Easily?

Pioneer Power Solutions seems to be in a fairly good position, in terms of cash burn, but we still think it's worthwhile considering how easily it could raise more money if it wanted to. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. Many companies end up issuing new shares to fund future growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

Pioneer Power Solutions has a market capitalisation of US$23m and burnt through US$8.1m last year, which is 35% of the company's market value. When Might Bonterra Resources Run Out Of Money?

A company's cash runway is the amount of time it would take to burn through its cash reserves at its current cash burn rate. As at September 2026, Bonterra Resources had cash of CA$15m and no debt. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through CA$13m. So it had a cash runway of approximately 14 months from September 2026. While that cash runway isn't too concerning, sensible holders would be peering into the distance, and considering what happens if the company runs out of cash. Because Bonterra Resources isn't currently generating revenue, we consider it an early-stage business. Over the last year its cash burn actually increased by a very significant 89%. While this spending increase is no doubt intended to drive growth, if the trend continues the company's cash runway will shrink very quickly. Bonterra Resources makes us a little nervous due to its lack of substantial operating revenue. We prefer most of the stocks on this list of stocks that analysts expect to grow.

Bonterra Resources has a market capitalisation of CA$46m and burnt through CA$13m last year, which is 28% of the company's market value. data.title: Insiders At Pacific Biosciences of California Sold US$1.3m In Stock, Alluding To Potential Weakness
data.description:
In the last year, many Pacific Biosciences of California, Inc. (NASDAQ:PACB) insiders sold a substantial stake in the company which may have sparked shareholders' attention. When evaluating insider transactions, knowing whether insiders are buying is usually more beneficial than knowing whether they are selling, as the latter can be open to many interpretations. However, when multiple insiders sell stock over a specific duration, shareholders should take notice as that could possibly be a red flag.

While we would never suggest that investors should base their decisions solely on what the directors of a company have been doing, we do think it is perfectly logical to keep tabs on what insiders are doing.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Pacific Biosciences of California

The Senior Business Advisor & Director, Christian O. Henry, made the biggest insider sale in the last 12 months. That single transaction was for US$752k worth of shares at a price of US$1.63 each. So it's clear an insider wanted to take some cash off the table, even slightly below the current price of US$1.63. We generally consider it a negative if insiders have been selling, especially if they did so below the current price, because it implies that they considered a lower price to be reasonable. Please do note, however, that sellers may have a variety of reasons for selling, so we don't know for sure what they think of the stock price. This single sale was just 28% of Christian O. Henry's stake.

In the last year Pacific Biosciences of California insiders didn't buy any company stock. The chart below shows insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year. If you click on the chart, you can see all the individual transactions, including the share price, individual, and the date!

See our latest analysis for Pacific Biosciences of California

If you like to buy stocks that insiders are buying, rather than selling, then you might just love this free list of companies. (Hint: Most of them are flying under the radar).

Pacific Biosciences of California Insiders Are Selling The Stock

Over the last three months, we've seen a bit of insider selling at Pacific Biosciences of California. insider Kathy Ordonez only netted US$33k selling shares, in that period. It's not great to see insider selling, nor the lack of recent buyers. But the volume sold is so low that it really doesn't bother us.

Insider Ownership Of Pacific Biosciences of California

Many investors like to check how much of a company is owned by insiders. Usually, the higher the insider ownership, the more likely it is that insiders will be incentivised to build the company for the long term. Our data indicates that Pacific Biosciences of California insiders own about US$5.2m worth of shares (which is 1.0% of the company). Overall, this level of ownership isn't that impressive, but it's certainly better than nothing!

So What Does This Data Suggest About Pacific Biosciences of California Insiders?

While there has not been any insider buying in the last three months, there has been selling. But the sales were small, so we're not concerned. Recent insider selling makes us a little nervous, in light of the broader picture of Pacific Biosciences of California insider transactions. And usually insiders own more stock in the company, according to our data. So while it's helpful to know what insiders are doing in terms of buying or selling, it's also helpful to know the risks that a particular company is facing.
